paper.title: Explore First, Exploit Next: The True Shape of Regret in Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit over an arbitrary model D
unmapped: Arbitrary (possibly non-parametric) model D of distributions over R with an expectation; bounds stated via K_inf relative to D
Large-T results require D to be 'well behaved' (K_inf locally Lipschitz in its second argument)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a bandit model $\mathcal{D}$, i.e., a collection of possible distributions $\nu_a$ associated with the arms. (That is, $\mathcal{D}$ is a subset of the set of all possible distributions over $\R$ with an expectation.)

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit model M([0,1]) of all distributions over [0,1] (distribution-free)
settings.definition_quote: Consider the bandit model $\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ of all probability distributions over $[0,1]$.

unmapped: Lower-bound instances N(0,1) vs N(-Delta,1) and N(0,1),N(0,1)

Sub-Gaussian K-armed bandit with known mu_star
settings.definition_quote: We consider the sub-Gaussian framework described in Section~\ref{sec:other-blb} and restrict our attention to the case when $\mu^\star$ is known.

algorithms.name: Algorithm with bounded regret, thanks to the knowledge of mu_star (Algorithm 1)

bound.regime: T -> infinity; quantity is E[N_a(T)]/log(T) for a suboptimal arm a

extra_assumptions: strategy uniformly fast convergent on D: E[N_a(T)] = o(T^alpha) for all alpha in (0,1]

source.label: th:asympt
source.quote: For all models $\mathcal{D}$, for all uniformly fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \[ \liminf_{T \to \infty} \,\, \frac{\E_{\unu} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr]}{\ln T} \geq \frac{1}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}\,. \]

results.notes: Re-derivation of the Burnetas-Katehakis bound with a new short proof and without the mild conditions on D; marked is_new false since the result is known. Bound is on expected pull count of a suboptimal arm normalized by log T.

bound.regime: all T >= 1; bound on expected number of pulls of arm a

extra_assumptions: strategy smarter than the uniform strategy: E[N_{a*}(T)] >= T/K for all optimal arms and all T

source.label: th:2
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are smarter than the uniform strategy on $\cD$, for all bandit problems~$\unu$, for all arms $a$, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \E_{\unu} \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{T}{K} \Bigl( 1 - \sqrt{2 T \Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)} \Bigr)\,. \]

results.notes: Absolute lower bound on pull count; regret lower bound follows by multiplying by gaps.

extra_assumptions: strategy smarter than the uniform strategy
results.notes: Linear initial phase for pull counts.

bound.regime: all T >= 1; holds unless E[N_a(T)] >= T/K

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms
results.notes: Either/or statement: either pull count >= T/K or the expected ratio of (clipped) pull counts of suboptimal vs optimal arm is lower bounded as recorded. In particular, for T <= K/(32 KL), ratio >= 1/2. KL_i is KL(nu_a, nu_{a*}).

bound.regime: all T; bound on total expected pulls of suboptimal arms

symbols.A_star: number of optimal arms of the bandit problem
symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on D

source.label: th:4
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\cD$, suboptimal arms are collectively sampled at least \sum_{a \not\in \cA^\star(\unu)} \E_{\unu}\bigl[N_{\psi,a}(T)\bigr]\geq T \Bigg(1-\frac{A^\star_{\unu}}{K} -\frac{A^\star_{\unu} \sqrt{ 2T \, \cK^{\max}_{\unu}}}{K}-\frac{2 A^\star_{\unu} T \cK^{\max}_{\unu}}{K}\Bigg)

results.notes: Regret lower bound follows via multiplication by min gap (eq. LBth4).

symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on D

bound.regime: T >= 2 large enough that (ln T)^{-4} < eps_D(mu_star) and a_T, b_T, c_T < 1

symbols.b_T: C_psi_D * H(nu) * ln(T)/T with H(nu)=sum over suboptimal arms of 1/Delta_a^2
symbols.C_psi_D: uniform super-fast convergence constant: E[N_a(T)] <= C_psi_D ln T / Delta_a^2

extra_assumptions: strategy uniformly super-fast convergent on D
model D well behaved (K_inf locally Lipschitz in second argument)

source.label: th:LBlargeT-NA
source.quote: For all uniformly super-fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on well-behaved models $\mathcal{D}$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\mathcal{D}$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \E_{\unu} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{\ln T}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)} \bigl( 1 - (a_T + b_T + c_T) \bigr) - \frac{\ln 2}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}

results.notes: Non-asymptotic: ln T/Kinf - O(ln ln T).

bound.regime: eps in (0,1/2); exists Bernoulli instance (1/2 for all arms but one at 1/2+eps)

source.label: th:distr-free
source.quote: For all $\varepsilon \in (0,1/2)$, for all strategies $\psi$, there exists a bandit problem $\unu'$ in $\mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ such that \[ R_{\psi,\unu',T} \geq T \varepsilon \left( 1 - \frac{1}{K} - \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{T}{K} \ln \frac{1}{1-4\varepsilon^2}} \right). \]

results.notes: Re-proof of Theorem A.2 of Auer et al. (2002); not new. Theorem number in appendix not printed explicitly; eps here is the construction parameter.

extra_assumptions: strategy symmetric in the sense E_{nu_0}[N_1(T)] = E_{nu_0}[N_2(T)] = T/2 on (N(0,1),N(0,1))

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: For all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sym}, for all $\Delta > 0$, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \E_{\unu_{\!\Delta}} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,2}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{1}{\Delta^2 + 1/T} \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad R_{\psi,\unu_{\!\Delta},T} \geq \frac{\Delta}{\Delta^2 + 1/T}\,. \]

results.notes: Well-chosen instance lower bound in the known-mu_star framework; also gives E[N_2] >= 1/(Delta^2+1/T). Theorem number not printed in source.

extra_assumptions: strategy symmetric in the sense of eq. (sym) (used via E_{nu_0}[N_2]=T/2 in proof)

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: In addition, for all strategies $\psi$ and for all $T$ such that $\E_{\unu_{\!\Delta}} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,2}(T) \bigr] \geq 1$, ... R_{\psi,\unu_{\!\Delta},T} \geq \min\left\{ \frac{2 (\ln 2) \Delta}{\Delta^2 + 2 \ln(4T)/T}, \,\, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \right\}.

results.notes: Statement says 'for all strategies' but proof uses symmetry assumption (E_{nu_0}[N_2]=T/2); algorithm_class ambiguous.

bound.regime: all T >= 1; max over the two instances (N(0,1),N(-Delta,1)) and (N(0,1),N(Delta,1))

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: Then, for all strategies $\psi$, for all $T \geq 1$, \max \bigl\{ R_{\psi,\unu_1,T}, \, R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \bigr\} \geq \min \! \left\{ \frac{W\bigl(T \Delta^2/1.2\bigr)}{2 \Delta}, \,\, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \right\}.

results.notes: Variant of Bubeck-Perchet-Rigollet Theorem 6; asymptotically weaker by factor 2 but nonnegative for all T.

extra_assumptions: strategy symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: Or, alternatively, for all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ R_{\psi,\unu_1,T} = R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \geq \frac{W\bigl(T \Delta^2/1.2\bigr)}{2 \Delta}\,. \]

source.label: th:finiteRegret:mus:known
source.quote: For all bandit problems $\unu = (\nu_a)_{a = 1,\ldots,K}$ where each distribution $\nu_a$ is sub-Gaussian in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sub-Gaussian}, the regret of the algorithm above is bounded by \[ R_{\unu,T} \leq \sum_{a : \Delta_a > 0} \Biggl( \frac{36\ln(17/\Delta_a)}{\Delta_a} + 3\Delta_a \Biggr). \]

results.notes: Bounded regret independent of T. Paper says refinement of BPR results 'already known by these authors'; algorithm inspired by BPR Algorithm 1.
